claims.text: A thin, Ni-rich transition layer inserted between HEA multilayers will enhance interface coherency.
Enhanced interface coherency will mediate a transition from diffusion-controlled creep toward dislocation-mediated creep.
HEA multilayers without an engineered transition layer exhibit ambiguous or diffusion-dominated creep because their interface coherency is less controlled.
A thin, Ni-rich interlayer should be introduced at the interfaces between HEA layers.
The proposed effect is expected under high-temperature creep conditions with sustained mechanical stress.
Diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms are both active under the proposed conditions.
The Ni-rich transition phase will have lattice parameters closely matching those of the adjacent HEA layers.
Close lattice-parameter matching by the Ni-rich phase will form highly coherent interfaces.
The Ni-rich layer will reduce lattice mismatch at HEA multilayer interfaces.
Reduced lattice mismatch will lower the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
Lowering the barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion will produce a gradual transition from diffusion-controlled to dislocation-mediated creep as temperature and stress increase.
HEA multilayers containing the Ni-rich interlayer will exhibit lower high-temperature creep strain rates than controls without the interlayer.
Samples containing the Ni-rich interlayer will show clearer evidence of dislocation activity than controls.
The beneficial effect will persist only while the Ni-rich layer maintains interface coherency.
Excessively high temperatures or prolonged exposure beyond a critical threshold may degrade the Ni-rich interlayer and diminish its mediating effect.

contradictions.description: Interlayer degradation at sufficiently severe temperature or exposure is presented as an expected boundary of the hypothesis, but the falsification rule also treats degradation of interface coherency as falsifying the hypothesis rather than as operation outside its stated boundary.
